title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

questions.prompt: Which event started World War II in Europe?
What is the name of the policy of giving in to an aggressive country's demands to avoid war?
Which countries were the main Axis powers?
Who was South Africa's Prime Minister during World War II?
Match each event to its year.
What was Blitzkrieg and why was it successful at first?
questions.memo:
✓ 'Lightning war': fast, surprise attacks using tanks and aircraft together (1)
✓ Enemies could not organise their defences in time (1)

questions.prompt: Who was Job Maseko and why is he remembered?
questions.memo:
✓ A black South African soldier captured at Tobruk (1)
✓ He sank a German ship using a home-made explosive and was awarded the Military Medal (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Nazi Germany and the Holocaust
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Source F: Words attributed to Pastor Martin Niemöller (adapted)
context.text:
First they came for the communists, and I did not speak out, because I was not a communist.
Then they came for the trade unionists, and I did not speak out, because I was not a trade unionist.
Then they came for the Jews, and I did not speak out, because I was not a Jew.
Then they came for me, and there was no one left to speak for me.

options: Took away German citizenship from Jews

questions.prompt: What name is given to the night in November 1938 when synagogues and Jewish shops were attacked?

pairs.right: Overcrowded area where Jews were forced to live

questions.prompt: Name TWO groups, other than Jews, who were persecuted by the Nazis.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): Roma and Sinti; people with disabilities; political opponents/communists; gay men; Jehovah's Witnesses; Slavs/Poles/Soviet prisoners

questions.prompt: Which party won the 1948 election and introduced apartheid?
Who became Prime Minister in 1948?
Which law divided towns into separate residential areas for each race?
What was the nickname of the reference book that black South Africans had to carry?
The Natives Land Act was passed in 1913, before apartheid began.
Match each law to what it did.
Name ONE place from which people were forcibly removed and explain why.
questions.memo:
✓ Sophiatown / District Six / Cato Manor (1)

questions.prompt: Explain why 'separate development' was not equal development.
questions.memo:

✓ Other groups received far less and had no political rights (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Resistance to Apartheid in the 1950s
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Source H: Extract from the Freedom Charter, 1955
context.text:
We, the People of South Africa, declare for all our country and the world to know: that South Africa belongs to all who live in it, black and white, and that no government can justly claim authority unless it is based on the will of all the people.

The People Shall Govern!
All National Groups Shall have Equal Rights!
The People Shall Share in the Country's Wealth!
The Land Shall be Shared Among Those Who Work It!
All Shall be Equal Before the Law!
All Shall Enjoy Equal Human Rights!
There Shall be Work and Security!
The Doors of Learning and Culture Shall be Opened!
There Shall be Houses, Security and Comfort!
There Shall be Peace and Friendship!

questions.prompt: Read Source H. (a) According to the Charter, to whom does South Africa belong? (b) Choose ONE clause and explain how it challenged apartheid.
questions.memo:
(a) ✓ All who live in it, black and white (1)
(b) ✓ Names a clause (1) ✓ explains how it opposed an apartheid law, e.g. 'The Doors of Learning shall be Opened' challenged Bantu Education (1)

questions.prompt: How did the Programme of Action of 1949 change the ANC's methods?
questions.memo:
✓ Earlier the ANC used petitions and deputations (1)
✓ Now it used mass action: boycotts, strikes and civil disobedience (1)
